title: A finite basis containing one for the coefficient subring
statement: Let p be prime, k a field of characteristic p, and (t_i) indexed by I a p-basis: the bounded finitely supported monomials form a basis over k^p. Let n,m be nonnegative integers and J a finite subset of I. Let kJ be the subfield generated by k^p and t_i for i outside J. In A = k[[x_1,...,x_n]][y_1,...,y_m], let S be the subring consisting exactly of elements whose coefficients lie in kJ and whose nonzero coefficients have every x and y exponent divisible by p. Then there exist d in N, an S-module basis b : Fin d -> A, and i : Fin d with b i = 1. This is a basis as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] over [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P5 (lemma-power-series-ring-subfields, line 11521) and its proof; properties (2)-(4) are conditions (1)-(3) of Lemma Tag 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), written out; tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: The k^p-span of bounded p-basis monomials avoiding J is exactly kJ. Products reduce exponents modulo p; a nonzero element lies in a finite-dimensional subring on finitely many generators, whose injective multiplication map is surjective and supplies its inverse. Splitting supports into J and its complement, uniqueness of the original p-basis coordinates gives the bounded J-monomial kJ-basis of k. See the full proof in the declaration docstring.

Divide each x and y exponent by p with remainder. Group coefficients in the finite field basis from the preceding step. Each grouped column has p-divisible exponents and coefficients in kJ, hence belongs to S. Only finitely many polynomial columns occur. Comparing coefficients proves independence and spanning of the monomials t^E x^e y^g with E supported in J and all exponents below p. Their index set is finite and contains the monomial 1. Enumerate by Fin d. See the complete construction and uniqueness argument in the docstring.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07P5 proof; parent steps 3--5, explicit coefficient and bounded-monomial arguments expanded in Lean docstring

theorem powerSeriesSubringFiniteBasis
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (I : Type w) (t : I → k)
    (hpb : ∃ b : Module.Basis
      {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}
      (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k => x ^ p))) k,
      ∀ E, b E = (E : I →₀ ℕ).prod (fun i e => t i ^ e))
    (n m : ℕ) (J : Finset I) (kJ : Subfield k)
    (hkJ : kJ = Subfield.closure
      (Set.range (fun x : k => x ^ p) ∪ {x : k | ∃ i : I, i ∉ J ∧ t i = x}))
    (S : Subring (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)))
    (hS : ∀ f, f ∈ S ↔
      ∀ (a : Fin n →₀ ℕ) (g : Fin m →₀ ℕ),
        MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ∈ kJ ∧
        (MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ≠ 0 →
          (∀ i, p ∣ a i) ∧ (∀ j, p ∣ g j))) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) S
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))) (i : Fin d), b i = 1
